name: New World Cider
overallimpression: A refreshing, crisp drink of substance with noticeable apple character, balanced acidity, and a clean finish. Can range from bone dry to delightfully sweet, but never bland or watery.
aroma: Prominent apple character ranging from fresh culinary apple fruitiness to subtle fermentation esters. Sweet versions will have more fresh apple juice character, while dry versions are more vinous and wine-like. Clean fermentation profile with no diacetyl, sulfur, or phenolic flaws.
appearance: Clear to brilliant clarity, though cloudy unfiltered examples exist. Color ranges from very pale straw to deep gold. Carbonation can range from still (no carbonation) to pétillant to champagne-like sparkling with a lively bead.
flavor: Noticeable apple flavor that reflects table or culinary fruit. Acidity is medium to high, providing crispness without being harsh or biting. Sweetness varies from bone-dry to sweet. Light bitterness or astringency from apple skins or seeds may be present, but tannic character should remain restrained.
mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with a clean, refreshing feel. May exhibit light tannin providing slight astringency, but no heavy puckering. Carbonation ranges from completely still to lively sparkling.
comments: Formerly known as Common Cider. Made primarily from culinary or table apples (such as McIntosh, Golden Delicious, Jonathan, Winesap, or Gala). Wild, crab, or heirloom apples may be blended in for improved acid and tannin balance.
history: Modern revival style popular throughout North America, Australia, and New Zealand, rooted in historical homestead farm ciders.
characteristicingredients: Culinary or table apples, wild or crab apples for acidity/tannin balance, clean wine, ale, or cider yeast strains.
stylecomparison: Comparable to a crisp white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc, but distinguished by pure, fresh apple varietal flavors.
commercialexamples: Angry Orchard Stone Dry, Farnum Hill Farmhouse Cider, Crispin Natural, Tieton Cider Works Wild Washington Apple

name: English Cider
overallimpression: A complex, full-bodied, traditional cider dominated by tannic astringency, rich bittersweet apple character, and earthy farmhouse complexity.
aroma: Earthy, rustic, and aromatic with rich apple character. Fermentation aromatics often include spicy, buttery, or farmhouse nuances from spontaneous fermentation or malolactic fermentation (MLF). No harsh chemical flaws or solvent notes.
appearance: Slightly cloudy to brilliantly clear. Deep yellow to dark golden amber color. Often still to lightly carbonated (pétillant), though sparkling commercial examples exist.
flavor: Complex, drying, and astringent with significant mouth-puckering tannins. Acidity is moderate to low, allowing bitter and astringent bittersweet apple tannins to take center stage. Residual sugar is typically low (bone dry to medium-dry).
mouthfeel: Medium to full body with notable tannic astringency and mouth-coating richness. Alcohol warmth is gentle but noticeable in higher-strength examples.
comments: Traditional farmhouse cider from the West Country of England (Somerset, Herefordshire, Gloucestershire). Bittersweet and bitter-sharp cider varieties give English cider its signature tannic backbone.
history: Centuries-old English cider-making tradition dating back to medieval orchards and estate cider presses.
characteristicingredients: Specialized English cider apples (bittersweet varieties like Dabinett, Kingston Black, Yarlington Mill, Chisel Jersey), native microflora or cultured yeast.
stylecomparison: Much more tannic, earthy, and austere than New World Cider; less fruity and sweeter than French Cidre.
commercialexamples: Aspall Draught Cyder, Dunkertons Black Fox, Henney's Dry, Weston's Old Rosie, Sheppy's Vintage
tags: standard-cider, english, bittersweet-apples, tannic, farmhouse, rustic

name: French Cider
overallimpression: A luscious, fruit-forward, aromatic traditional cider with deep amber color, rich unfermented apple sweetness, gentle warming alcohol, and balanced bittersweet tannins.
aroma: Intense ripe, cooked, or caramelized apple aromatics with rich fruity esters. Distinctive rustic, buttery, and earthy nuances are common from keeving and long, cool fermentations.
appearance: Luminous yellow-gold to deep rich amber or copper. Generally clear to brilliant with an effervescent, fine mousse-like carbonation bead.
flavor: Rich, sweet, and complex apple flavor with caramel, baked apple, or honey notes. Acidity is moderate and pleasantly refreshing, countering the sweet residual sugars. Moderate to high tannins provide roundness and structured astringency without harshness.
mouthfeel: Medium to full mouthfeel with a creamy, smooth texture from natural unfermented sugars. Carbonation is typically lively and sparkling, resembling fine Champagne.
comments: Traditional cidre from Normandy and Brittany produced via 'keeving' (maceration and pectin coagulation that depletes nutrients to naturally halt fermentation before dryness).
history: Protected geographical traditions in Northwestern France with centuries of dedicated orchard cultivation of bittersweet varietals.
characteristicingredients: French bittersweet and bitter-sharp apple varieties (Bedan, Michelin, Kermerrien, Frequin Rouge), natural wild fermentation or slow cider yeast.
stylecomparison: Sweeter, fruitier, and less astringent than English Cider; much richer and more tannic than New World Cider.
commercialexamples: Domaine Dupont Cidre Bouché Brut de Normandie, Etienne Dupont Organic Cidre, Eric Bordelet Sidre Tendre, Manoir de Kinkiz
tags: standard-cider, french, keeving, bittersweet, sparkling, rich

name: New World Perry
overallimpression: A delicate, refreshing, pale beverage crafted from culinary/table pears, displaying subtle pear aromatics, crisp acidity, and a light, clean, wine-like finish.
aroma: Delicate and floral pear aromatics with clean fruit character. Soft citrus or floral blossoms may be detected. No harsh sulfur, phenolic smoke, or solvent faults.
appearance: Very pale straw to light yellow with greenish highlights. Excellent clarity. Still to highly carbonated.
flavor: Gentle, clean pear fruitiness with supportive acidity. Residual sweetness ranges from dry to sweet, often with a hint of perceived residual sugar due to natural unfermentable sorbitol. Very clean and wine-like.
mouthfeel: Light to medium body. Soft on the palate with minimal to no tannic astringency. Refreshing and crisp.
comments: Crafted from culinary or dessert pears (such as Bartlett, Bosc, D'Anjou, or Comice) rather than dedicated perry pear cultivars.
history: Modern American and Australasian development answering the demand for clean, accessible pear fermentations.
characteristicingredients: Culinary/table pears, wine or cider yeast, yeast nutrients to ensure complete and healthy fermentation.
stylecomparison: Much lighter, cleaner, and less tannic or acidic than Traditional Perry; softer and more floral than New World Cider.
commercialexamples: Tieton Cider Works Sparkling Perry, Snowdrift Perry, ACE Perry Hard Cider, Seattle Cider Perry

name: Traditional Perry
overallimpression: A complex, austere, and highly structured beverage crafted exclusively from true perry pears, showcasing pronounced tannins, intense acidity, and unfermentable sorbitol body.
aroma: Complex floral and varietal pear aromatics, often accompanied by rustic, earthy, citrus, or leather nuances. Distinctive wood, spice, or farmhouse traits from wild fermentation.
appearance: Pale straw to deep gold. Clarity can range from crystal clear to slight haze due to sorbitol and complex tannins.
flavor: Profound sensory balance between high natural acidity, astringent pear tannins, and residual sweetness from unfermentable sorbitol. Authentic perry pear varietal character is pronounced and lingering.
mouthfeel: Full and viscous with noticeable astringency and mouth-coating tannic grip. High sorbitol content provides substantial body despite high attenuation.
comments: True perry is among the most demanding beverages to produce, relying on ancient, slow-growing perry pear trees whose fruit is completely inedible raw.
history: Centuries-old heritage centered in the Three Counties of England (Gloucestershire, Herefordshire, Worcestershire) and the Mayenne/Normandy regions of France.
characteristicingredients: True perry pear varieties (such as Thorn, Hendre Huffcap, Blakeney Red, Yellow Huffcap, Butt), wild or wine yeast.
stylecomparison: Substantially more tannic, acidic, and viscous than New World Perry. Has sensory parallels to aged white Burgundy or dry Riesling.
commercialexamples: Tom Oliver's Traditional Perry, Dunkertons Perry, Minchew Blakeney Red Perry, Eric Bordelet Poire Granit
tags: standard-perry, traditional, perry-pears, tannic, sorbitol, complex, heritage

name: New England Cider
overallimpression: A strong, robust, warming cider enriched with adjunct sugars and raisins, featuring deep caramelized complexity, wood or barrel aging notes, and high alcohol strength.
aroma: Rich apple aromas intertwined with dark brown sugar, molasses, honey, or caramel. Raisin, dried plum, or dark dried fruit notes are common. Oak or spirit barrel notes may be present.
appearance: Medium yellow to deep rich amber or mahogany. Clarity is good to brilliant. Carbonation ranges from still to pétillant or sparkling.
flavor: Rich and substantial with complex caramelized sugar, molasses, or raisin notes complementing assertive apple acidity. Alcohol warmth is prominent but smooth. Tannins from apple skins and oak provide balanced astringency.
mouthfeel: Medium-full to full body with warming alcohol and chewy texture. Astringency is moderate, balanced by residual sugars and alcohol viscosity.
comments: An authentic North American historic style developed by early colonists who boosted cider gravities with local brown sugar, molasses, and raisins to withstand winter storage.
history: Developed in colonial New England orchards where harsh winters necessitated high-alcohol, preservative-rich estate ciders.
characteristicingredients: New England heirloom apples (Baldwin, Northern Spy, Roxbury Russet), brown sugar, molasses, raisins, oak cask aging, ale or wine yeast.
stylecomparison: Much stronger, darker, and more caramel/molasses-forward than Standard New World Cider. Resembles an English Barleywine or fortified cider.
commercialexamples: Woodchuck 802 Dark & Dry, Farnum Hill Extra Dry with Raisins, Snowdrift Cornice, Abandoned Hard Cider Classic
tags: specialty-cider, new-england, strong, molasses, raisins, barrel-aged, warming

name: Cider with Other Fruit
overallimpression: A harmonious blend of apple cider and other complementary fruits (berries, stone fruit, cherries, citrus, or tropical fruit), where apple character remains evident and fruit elevates the whole.
aroma: Enticing combination of crisp apple character and vibrant complementary fruit aromatics. Neither the fruit nor the cider should completely overpower the other.
appearance: Color is dictated by the fruit used (ruby red from raspberries, garnet from cherries, orange-pink from peaches). Clarity is generally good, though fruit pectins can cause mild haze.
flavor: Crisp apple cider foundation seamlessly integrated with real fruit flavor and supportive fruit acidity. Sweetness ranges from bone dry to sweet dessert levels, balanced by fruit tartness.
mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body. Fruit tannins (such as from berry skins or cherry pits) may contribute delicate astringency.
comments: Common fruits include blackberries, raspberries, cherries, blackcurrants, peaches, cranberries, and blueberries. Artificial syrup flavorings are a defect.
history: Popular craft cidery staple combining regional seasonal orchard harvests with fresh orchard fruits.
characteristicingredients: Culinary or cider apples, whole fruit, 100% pure fruit purees or unpasteurized fruit juices, clean fermenting yeast.
stylecomparison: Distinct from pure cider due to obvious fruit addition; distinct from pure fruit wine or fruit mead due to cider base and lower gravity.
commercialexamples: Citizen Cider The Dirty Mayor, Seattle Cider Blackberry, Original Sin Black Cider, Schilling Grapefruit Chill
tags: specialty-cider, fruit-cider, berries, cherry, vibrant, tart

name: Applewine
overallimpression: A high-alcohol, wine-like cider produced by boosting apple juice gravity with neutral fermentable sugars, resulting in a crisp, clean, vinous beverage resembling a white wine.
aroma: Clean and vinous with delicate apple fruitiness and noticeable alcohol warmth. Lacks the heavy caramel, molasses, or spice notes of New England Cider.
appearance: Pale straw to deep gold. Brilliant clarity is expected. Often still to lightly carbonated (pétillant), though sparkling versions exist.
flavor: Dry to semi-dry finish with crisp malic acidity, clean fermented apple character, and pleasant alcohol warmth. High attenuation yields a clean, elegant profile without cloying residual sweetness.
mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body with warming alcohol. Smooth and wine-like on the palate with minimal astringency.
comments: Unlike New England Cider, adjunct sugars are strictly neutral (cane sugar, corn sugar, or concentrated apple juice) rather than flavorful molasses or brown sugar.
history: Traditional American homebrewing and winemaking adaptation seeking table-wine strengths from orchard apples.
characteristicingredients: High-acid culinary apples, cane or dextrose sugar to boost gravity, wine or Champagne yeast.
stylecomparison: Much more vinous and alcoholic than standard New World Cider; lighter in color and adjunct complexity than New England Cider.
commercialexamples: Warwick Valley Apple Wine, Lyman Orchards Apple Wine, Lynfred Apple Wine
tags: specialty-cider, applewine, high-alcohol, vinous, crisp, clean

name: Ice Cider
overallimpression: A luscious, intensely sweet, high-gravity dessert cider concentrated by freezing temperatures, balanced by vivid, piercing natural malic acidity.
aroma: Explosive, concentrated apple aromatics: baked apples, apple pie, honey, apricot, and candied lemon peel. Alcohol warmth is noticeable but velvety and smooth.
appearance: Brilliant yellow-gold to deep amber and copper. High viscosity forms thick legs on the glass. Typically still to lightly pétillant.
flavor: Unctuous, rich, concentrated apple sweetness countered by intense natural acidity. Notes of peach, apricot, caramel, honey, and baked fruit. Finish is long, decadent, and clean without cloying heaviness.
mouthfeel: Full, velvety, and luxurious body with viscous mouthfeel. Alcohol warmth is comforting and well integrated.
comments: Concentration is achieved either via cryo-extraction (freezing apples on the branch before pressing) or cryo-concentration (freezing fresh juice and draining the concentrated sugar-rich nectar).
history: Pioneered in Quebec, Canada in the 1990s by cidermaker Christian Barthomeuf, quickly becoming an internationally acclaimed luxury dessert beverage.
characteristicingredients: Late-harvest winter apples (McIntosh, Spartan, Cortland), cold winter ambient temperatures, slow alcohol-tolerant wine yeast.
stylecomparison: Parallels luxury Ice Wine (Eiswein) or Sauternes, but defined by pure, opulent apple essence.
commercialexamples: Eden Deep Cut Ice Cider, Domaine Pinnacle Ice Cider, Neige Première Cidre de Glace
tags: specialty-cider, ice-cider, dessert, concentrated, cryo-extraction, luxury

name: Cider with Herbs/Spices
overallimpression: A harmonious blend of crisp apple cider and culinary herbs, spices, or botanicals (cinnamon, ginger, vanilla, hops, or chili peppers), where the botanicals accentuate and complement the apple base.
aroma: Distinctive aromatic herbs, warm spices, or floral hop character layered over a clean apple base. Spices should smell fresh and aromatic, not artificial or medicinal.
appearance: Pale straw to deep amber. Spices may impart subtle hues or slight haze. Carbonation ranges from still to sparkling.
flavor: Crisp apple flavor melded with botanical or spice character. Cinnamon, allspice, and nutmeg offer warming cider notes; hops provide citrus/floral aroma and delicate bitterness; ginger or peppers contribute zesty heat.
mouthfeel: Medium-light to medium body. Spices (like ginger or chilies) may contribute warming or tingling sensations on the palate.
comments: Includes spiced holiday ciders, dry-hopped ciders, and botanical infusions. Key requirement is seamless balance: no single spice should overpower drinkability.
history: Centuries of spiced mulled cider (Wassail) combined with contemporary craft dry-hopping techniques.
characteristicingredients: Culinary or cider apples, natural culinary spices (cinnamon, clove, ginger, vanilla), brewing hops, botanicals, clean yeast.
stylecomparison: Similar to spiced beer or metheglin mead, but on a crisp, refreshing, low-tannin cider base.
commercialexamples: Finnriver Dry Hopped Cider, Citizen Cider The Lake Hopper, Bold Rock Spiced Cider, Seattle Cider Basil Mint
tags: specialty-cider, spiced-cider, dry-hopped, botanical, seasonal, wassail

name: Specialty Cider/Perry
overallimpression: An open-ended, innovative style for ciders or perries featuring non-standard ingredients, spirit barrel aging, wild fermentation cultures, or creative techniques that do not fit other categories.
aroma: Complex and idiosyncratic depending on specialty components (bourbon, rye, rum oak barrels, wild Brettanomyces funk, souring bacteria, or novel sugars like agave or maple syrup).
appearance: Variable depending on specialty ingredients and barrel aging, ranging from pale gold to dark copper.
flavor: Intriguing, innovative flavor profile where apple or pear character remains recognizable while integrating specialty barrel aging, wild yeast funk, or novel fermentables.
mouthfeel: Variable body depending on gravity and adjuncts. Barrel aging may contribute oak tannins and alcohol warmth.
comments: Encompasses barrel-aged ciders, sour/funky wild ciders, maple-sweetened ciders, smoked ciders, and experimental hybrid fermentations.
history: Pioneered by the modern craft cider revolution pushing the boundaries of orchard fermentation.
characteristicingredients: Apples or pears, spirit barrels (bourbon, gin, rum), wild yeast/microflora (Brettanomyces, Lactobacillus), unconventional sugars or wood additions.
stylecomparison: Analogous to Experimental Beer or Experimental Mead in modern competition structures.
commercialexamples: Angry Orchard The Muse, Virtue Cider The Mitten, Revered Spirits Bourbon Barrel Cider, Sea Cider Prohibition
